patches.old: - **Th2**: Driven by IL-4. Promotes B cell class switching to IgE and IgG1, eosinophil activation.
patches.new: - **Th2**: Driven by IL-4. Promotes B cell class switching to IgE (and to IgG4 in humans; the IgG1 association comes from mouse studies), eosinophil activation.
patches.reason: IL-4 drives switching to IgE and IgG4 in humans; IgG1 is the mouse counterpart.

patches.new: → susceptibility to catalase-positive organisms (e.g., the bacteria *Staphylococcus aureus*, *Burkholderia*, *Serratia* and *Nocardia*, and the fungus *Aspergillus*).

visual.title: Two arms of immunity, one coordinated response
visual.alt: A schematic graph of response size over days: the innate response rises within hours, the primary adaptive response peaks after one to two weeks with IgM first, and a secondary response after re-exposure is faster, larger and mostly IgG. Boxes list innate players (barriers, neutrophils, macrophages, NK cells, complement, dendritic cells with germline pattern-recognition receptors) and adaptive players (B and T cells with V(D)J-generated receptors and memory), linked by dendritic cells that provide peptide-MHC and co-stimulation in lymph nodes.
visual.caption: Curve shapes are schematic and only compare timing.
